because of the bright lights of the Romans.
The Persians, however, easily pierced with arrows those who carried the lights.
And when it was morning,
the king and his forces set up ladders and went up.
And for one day the citizens hemmed them in on that tower,
and they began to undermine the tower from below,
so that the Persians might collapse down.
Then the Persians took control of another tower,
and of another,
and others,
and they entered into the city {OCR?}.
And they opened the gates,
and they killed eighty thousand people in it.
Only the Church of the Forty Martyrs,
while full of people,
the kinglet of the Armenians seized it,
and he petitioned the king and saved it.
The king, moreover, sent the gold and silver and bronze down the Tigris river to his own country.
And of the people who were left, they additionally killed one out of ten,
because many of the Persians had been killed.
And they clothed Leontius and Cyrus, the judges of the city, in filthy garments,
and put pig-ropes around their necks,
and made them carry sows,
while proclaiming:
"Governors, it is said, who did not govern well,
and allowed the king to be insulted,
shall thus be insulted."
Now when King Anastasius heard these things,
he was grieved not a little.
Then he sent five generals against Nisibis,
but they were unable to capture it.
And he commanded that a city be built beside the mountain as a refuge for the army,
and it was built where Darius was killed,
and for that reason it was called Dara.
And it was completed in three years with wondrous buildings,
and was named Anastasiopolis.
Anastasius also made a statue on a column,
because that of Theodosius had fallen in that earthquake in which Neocaesarea also fell,
except for the church of Saint Gregory the Wonderworker;
and Rhodes also fell.
And the king sent gold so that they might dig out the corpses of the suffocated and bury them.
And the tyrant Vitalian rebelled,
and the king bound him and imprisoned him.
And in the twenty-second year of Anastasius, Armenia rebelled against the Romans.
And he sent forces against the Armenians and slaughtered many of them,
and brought Armenia back under the subjugation of the Romans.
And in the year 831 [of the Greeks],
(520 of our Lord?), he fell asleep in peace.
